mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, market expectations for future rate cuts increase, lowering the discount rate applied to equities and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds or signals hold in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day average preceding the trigger, or the 2-month FEDFUNDS stay above 5.25% is not sustained beyond 90 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by at least 0.5 percentage points within a single month signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10% AND UNRATE decreases by ≥0.5pp in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening after a period of softening
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE pattern recurs but results in negative or flat 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) of at least 5% for three consecutive months coincides with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of less than 2%, indicating resilient consumer spending while supply remains soft, which tends to support equity valuations and yields positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases ≥5% for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO decreases <2% over the same period
regime_hint: Resilient demand in a mildly contractionary supply environment
failure_condition: The pattern recurs but is followed by negative 20-day returns, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-sample t-test.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 8% in a single month, while consumer demand (HOUST) remains flat or slightly rising, suggests supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and compresses growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >8% in a single month AND HOUST increases ≤2% in the same month
regime_hint: Industrial contraction without concurrent demand recovery
failure_condition: The INDPRO contraction is not followed by negative returns within the 5-day horizon, or the effect is absorbed within 2 days.

mechanism_narrative: A surprise cut in the federal funds rate by more than 25 basis points in a single meeting, when the prior policy was already below 4%, generates a one-month positive S&P 500 20-day forward return by lowering financing costs and boosting risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by >25bp in a single month when last month FEDFUNDS < 4.00%
regime_hint: Unexpected easing in a low-rate environment
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 20-day window after the cut, or the effect is reversed in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months without a corresponding rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for four consecutive months AND PAYEMS does not increase by ≥1% in the same window
regime_hint: Labor market tightening without participation expansion
failure_condition: The pattern recurs but is followed by negative or flat 60-day forward returns, or wage growth (not directly observable) does not rise in line with the unemployment decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden and persistent drop in consumer inflation proxies (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months, while industrial production remains flat, signals a cooling demand environment that weighs on equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% for two consecutive months AND INDPRO remains unchanged
regime_hint: Demand cooling in a soft-supply environment
failure_condition: The CPIAUCSL decline is not followed by negative 20-day returns, or the effect is explained by supply-side factors (e.g., energy price shocks).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for 6 consecutive months), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs and reduced risk appetite, except when a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) occurs that signals a supply shock overriding the tightening effect.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for 6 consecutive months AND INDPRO decreases by ≥8% in the following quarter
failure_condition: The regime condition is met but a supply shock does not override the tightening effect, or the 60-day forward returns remain positive.
